chunks: The worst of your ministers is he who was a minister for the mischievous before you,
and who shared with them in sins, so let him not be your intimate companion.
for they are helpers of sinners and brothers of the oppressors.
and you will find among them good substitutes who have like their views and influence,
and upon them is not like their vices, burdens, and sins.
those who did not assist an oppressor in his oppression, nor a sinner in his sin.
those are lighter for you in cost, better for you in support, more tender towards you in affection, and less attached to others.
so take those as your special ones for your privacy and your public gatherings.

Then, let their most preferred among you be those who speak the bitter truth to you, and who assist you least in what occurs from you which Allah dislikes for His friends, even if that occurs from your desire where it occurred.
ai.seo_question: What are the criteria for selecting the best ministers according to Imam Ali in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this foundational directive from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (AS) distinguishes between mere administrative competence and moral integrity, warning that ministers who share in the ruler's sins become accomplices in injustice. He emphasizes selecting advisors who offer 'bitter truth' rather than flattery, ensuring they support divine will over the ruler's personal whims, a principle central to Shia political ethics regarding accountability and justice.
